taxonomy.label: software_bug
taxonomy.name: Software / OS bug
taxonomy.description: The message reports a software malfunction: an OS-update regression (slowdown, battery drain after update), a system or app bug, crash, freeze, glitch, or a feature that stopped working as expected.
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Usually auto-handlable with troubleshooting evidence; escalate when the user reports data loss or a bricked device.
examples: since new update my phone is running slow and battery drains
why when I type the letter I this box keeps popping up

taxonomy.label: device_hardware
taxonomy.name: Device / hardware fault
taxonomy.description: The message reports a physical-device problem: battery, screen, buttons, camera, speaker, charging, water damage, cracks, or a device that will not turn on / start.
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Auto-handle with troubleshooting evidence first; hardware damage usually ends in repair guidance (see repair_warranty).
examples: My MacBook Air won't start! Was fine last night
anyway you can run a remote test on my battery health?

taxonomy.label: account_icloud
taxonomy.name: Account / Apple ID / iCloud
taxonomy.description: Sign-in and account-access problems (Apple ID, password, verification codes, two-factor) and iCloud data problems (storage, backup, sync, restore, contacts/photos in the cloud).
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Account recovery steps are well covered by historical evidence; escalate on suspected takeover (see security_privacy).
examples: why won't one of my email accounts sign in?
why doesn't it let me turn on iCloud, I click it and nothing happens

taxonomy.label: connectivity
taxonomy.name: Connectivity
taxonomy.description: Wireless/network problems: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth pairing, cellular signal, hotspot, AirDrop, or general connection failures.
examples: There might be a bug in iPhone X and Bluetooth, keeps disconnecting from my car
started getting a "No Sim Card Installed" message

taxonomy.label: billing_purchases
taxonomy.name: Billing / purchases / orders
taxonomy.description: Anything commercial: charges and invoices, refunds and purchase problems, subscriptions and trials, and online-store orders/delivery/shipping.
taxonomy.eda_anchor: Billing (2.4%) + Refunds (1.5%) + Order/Delivery (1.0%) + Subscriptions (0.4%) — merged, see module docstring rule 2
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Refunds and account-bound purchases typically need a human agent with account access — default to escalation.
examples: just wasted $30 on a movie I can't even watch now
when is my order going to arrive

taxonomy.label: repair_warranty
taxonomy.name: Repair / warranty
taxonomy.description: Repair status and logistics, replacement requests, warranty coverage questions, Genius Bar / authorized service.
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Needs appointment/order lookups a historical-evidence agent cannot perform — escalate unless purely informational.
examples: I think I either scratched or cracked my Apple Watch

taxonomy.label: security_privacy
taxonomy.name: Security / privacy
taxonomy.description: Phishing and scam messages impersonating Apple, hacked or compromised accounts, stolen devices, privacy concerns.
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Safety-critical — always escalate to a human; never auto-generate account-security advice.
examples: This is spam right, I clicked verify your account and it took me to a webpage of apple ID

taxonomy.label: general_complaint
taxonomy.name: General complaint / venting
taxonomy.description: Dissatisfaction with Apple or a product/update WITHOUT any specific actionable issue, malfunction or request stated. If the message names a concrete problem, classify by that problem instead (e.g. software_bug, device_hardware).
taxonomy.eda_anchor: Part of the EDA unmatched pool (no keyword topic)
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Empathetic acknowledgement from evidence is fine; offer troubleshooting only if the user later states a concrete issue.
examples: IOS 11 has killed all the perks of having an iPhone

taxonomy.label: support_process
taxonomy.name: Support-process problem
taxonomy.description: Meta-complaints about reaching support itself: cannot reach a human, useless automated assistant, DM/chat channel problems, support page or phone-line issues.
taxonomy.eda_anchor: Part of the EDA unmatched pool (no keyword topic)
taxonomy.escalation_hint: The user is explicitly asking for a human — the clearest escalation trigger in the taxonomy.
examples: I'm trying to get into contact with someone from customer support, I need to speak to an actual person

taxonomy.label: other
taxonomy.name: Other / out of scope
taxonomy.description: Everything that fits no other class: pre-sales product questions (discounts, availability), ambiguous one-word messages, non-English messages that cannot be confidently classified, and off-topic content.
taxonomy.eda_anchor: Part of the EDA unmatched pool (no keyword topic)
taxonomy.escalation_hint: Heterogeneous by construction — default to escalation.

golden_set.sampling: uniform random sample, no rare-class boosting

labeling.labeler: project author — every message read and labelled by meaning; the worksheet shows no keyword hints to avoid biasing labels
labeling.validation: automated gate: every worksheet row labelled exactly once, labels restricted to taxonomy classes, no unknown ids (build exits non-zero on failure)

golden_set.split_strategy: conversation-level, stratified by label, seed 42 (ratios 70/15/15, per-class rounding to train)
golden_set.period_note: 99.5% of the 80,244 openers fall in Sep–Dec 2017 (the iOS 11 rollout window of the corpus), so the golden set — like the corpus itself — is dominated by iOS 11 era complaints. Metrics measure this historical window, not a balanced mix.

keyword_rules.description: Phase 1 EDA provisional keyword topics mapped onto taxonomy labels; word-boundary matching, first match in EDA topic order wins, no match -> other.

majority.description: Always predict the train majority class (software_bug).

tfidf_logreg.description: TfidfVectorizer(word 1-2 grams, English stopwords, sublinear tf) + LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000), fit on the train split; hyperparameters selected by 5-fold CV on the train split (criterion: mean of accuracy and macro-F1).
tfidf_logreg.selection_criterion: 5-fold CV on train: mean(accuracy, macro-F1); ties -> macro-F1. Validation is too small (n=29) for stable tuning and is kept as a held-out sanity check; test untouched until final evaluation.
